submitted.rationale: Index 8 (Pb0.52Sb0.48, near the Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore that MACE puts close to the hull) had the highest measured EQE: 0.0084%. The two other measurements were lower: index 0 gave -0.0012% and index 11 gave 0.0007%. All values are very small, so the ranking is uncertain.

rejected.reason: Pb-rich end; measured EQE about zero (-0.0012%).
Pyrochlore + PbSb2O6 region; measured 0.0007%, and GLLB predicts a 3.8 eV gap for PbSb2O6, too wide to absorb 2.7 eV light.

consultations.verdict: Support (weak): Pb2Sb2O7 pyrochlore near-stable per MACE (0.049 eV/atom above hull), matching Pb~0.5 composition. MEGNet HSE gap 0.49 eV looks unrealistic (Naples yellow is ~2.5 eV experimentally), so the gap is uninformative; PbSb2O6 at 2.69 eV sits at the 2.7 eV absorption edge. Measure index 8 as the pyrochlore anchor.

Mixed. PbSb2O6 is on the hull (MACE Ehull 0), but its predicted gap (2.69 eV) is marginal for 2.7 eV photons. For PbO, MEGNet predicts 3.36 eV, but experimental PbO gaps are ~1.9–2.7 eV, so PbO-rich films should absorb. Index 8 gave a low EQE (0.008%). Probe the Pb-rich end (index 0).

Weakly against pure PbSb2O6: the GLLB gap of 3.8 eV suggests it absorbs little at 2.7 eV. Still, the measured trend runs upward from the Pb-rich end (index 0 < index 8), and index 11 lies in the two-phase region between the pyrochlore and PbSb2O6, where a heterojunction could help. GP UCB also picks index 11, so I'll measure it.
